tagline: A research collective curating fully open reasoning datasets and recipes, from the OpenThoughts3 data recipe to the OpenThinker models.
about: OpenThoughts is a collaboration of researchers and engineers from universities including Stanford, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, NYU, the University of Washington and TUM, together with LAION. It launched publicly in January 2025 with the aim of producing open post-training data for reasoning models.

The project publishes datasets, training code and models together. Its OpenThoughts3 recipe, described in the paper "OpenThoughts: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models", was derived from more than 1,000 controlled experiments and produced the 1.2 million example OpenThoughts3 dataset and the OpenThinker3-7B model.

Compute and support come from academic centers such as the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, TACC and TU Dresden, as well as industry partners. From late 2025 the group extended its work to agentic tasks under the OpenThoughts-Agent project.
mission: OpenThoughts aims to make the data side of reasoning models as open as the weights, so that the community can study which data choices matter. It treats systematic, reproducible ablation of data pipelines as its main method.

tagline: A public benefit company building an unconditionally open platform for training, evaluating and deploying foundation models, with an open-source library at its core.
about: Oumi emerged from stealth in January 2025 with a $10 million seed round and an open-source platform covering the model lifecycle, from data preparation and training to evaluation and deployment. It was built with researchers from more than a dozen universities.

The company is led by co-founder and CEO Manos Koukoumidis, a former Google Cloud engineering manager, with co-founder Oussama Elachqar and other founders who say they worked on PaLM at Google. Oumi PBC publishes its core library as open source and has released models such as the HallOumi hallucination detector.
Alongside the open library, Oumi offers a commercial platform with an agent that automates evaluation, data curation and training for teams building specialized models.
mission: Oumi wants AI development to be collective and reproducible, with open code, data and models rather than closed stacks. It describes its aim as giving AI a shared, Linux-like open foundation.
known_for: Open library for training and evaluation

tagline: A Tehran-based developer of Persian-language models, known for the Dorna decoder LLMs and the TookaBERT and Tooka-SBERT encoders.
about: Part AI publishes open Persian-language models on Hugging Face. Its Dorna family consists of decoder-only models trained or fine-tuned on Persian data, including Dorna2 variants built on Llama 3.1.

Its encoder line includes TookaBERT in base and large sizes, described in an arXiv paper as a step forward for Persian language understanding, and the Tooka-SBERT sentence embedding models in small and large sizes.
The models serve Persian NLP developers and researchers who need open baselines for a language that is underrepresented in multilingual models.
mission: Part AI works to strengthen Persian language technology by releasing models and benchmarks that others can build on.

tagline: A robotics foundation-model company whose pi0 family of vision-language-action models and openpi code give robot learning a shared open baseline.
about: Physical Intelligence builds general-purpose foundation models for robots rather than robot hardware. The company was co-founded by Karol Hausman, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn and others, and draws on research from Google, UC Berkeley and Stanford.

Its pi0 model combines a vision-language backbone with a flow-matching action expert to generate robot actions. The company released pi0 weights and training and inference code through the openpi repository in early 2025.
Researchers and robotics developers use openpi to fine-tune policies on their own robots, which makes the project one of the main open entry points to robot foundation models.
mission: The company aims to build a general-purpose model that can control many kinds of robots across many tasks. It shares part of its research openly to help the field progress.

tagline: A Paris research company building language models and the Common Corpus dataset on openly licensed and rights-cleared data.
about: Pleias is based at Station F in Paris and develops tools around training data: Common Corpus, an open collection of public-domain and permissively licensed text, Synth for synthetic training data, and Stratum for structuring documents.

Common Corpus draws on government records, legal archives, scientific literature and multilingual sources, and is available on Hugging Face. The team has also trained small models, including a 600-million-parameter model for the Paris transport operator RATP.
The company's authors include Pierre-Carl Langlais and Anastasia Stasenko, and it publishes research and models openly.
mission: Pleias argues that capable models can be built on data with clear provenance and licensing. Its goal is to make that approach practical for industry and public institutions.

tagline: A Bordeaux robotics company building open-source robots such as Reachy and Reachy Mini, now part of Hugging Face.
about: Pollen Robotics was founded in 2016 in Bordeaux by two former researchers from Inria's Flowers team. It began with the open-source 3D-printed humanoid Poppy and later launched the Reachy robot at CES 2020.
In 2022 the company placed second in the ANA Avatar XPRIZE, and in April 2023 it raised a seed round of 2.4 million euros. Its current products include Reachy 2, Reachy Mini and the Microduck biped.
Reachy Mini, a small expressive robot for AI builders, is promoted with over 10,000 units shipped. The company's site and Hugging Face profile present it as part of Hugging Face.
mission: Pollen builds expressive, open robots so that AI builders and makers can experiment with embodied AI. It publishes software, models and datasets for robot control.

tagline: A University of Bonn project building open foundation models for low-resource languages, best known for the Tucano Portuguese models and the GigaVerbo corpus.
about: Polygl0t, also referred to as Project Polyglot, develops efficient language models for low-resource languages. It is funded by the German BMBF and the North Rhine-Westphalia ministry as part of TRA Sustainable Futures at the University of Bonn, and trains on Bonn's Marvin cluster and Jülich's JUPITER Booster.

Its Tucano models, first described in 2024, were trained on GigaVerbo, a corpus of about 200 billion deduplicated Portuguese tokens. The follow-up Tucano 2 paper of March 2026 introduces GigaVerbo-v2, with about 320 billion tokens, and models from roughly 0.5B to 3.7B parameters.
The group publishes weights, datasets and training code, including an LLM foundry repository and a fork of the evaluation harness.
mission: Polygl0t aims to close the linguistic divide in NLP by making capable open models for languages that large developers serve poorly.

tagline: A Simons Foundation and Flatiron Institute backed collaboration building open foundation models and datasets for scientific data.
about: Polymathic AI is led by principal investigator Shirley Ho and brings together researchers working across astrophysics, physics and machine learning. Its team includes Kyunghyun Cho, Miles Cranmer, Francois Lanusse and Michael McCabe.

The group builds machine learning models that share concepts across scientific disciplines and releases them for researchers worldwide. A scientific advisory group includes Yann LeCun, Leslie Greengard and David Spergel.
Recent news on its site covers agent systems for NMR structure elucidation and protein design.
mission: Polymathic AI wants to give scientists pretrained models that carry across fields, so new problems start from shared knowledge rather than from scratch.

tagline: A Tokyo deep learning company behind Chainer, the MN-Core accelerator and the PLaMo Japanese language models.
about: Preferred Networks was established in March 2014 as a spin-off from Preferred Infrastructure, founded in 2006. Toru Nishikawa is CEO and Daisuke Okanohara is COO.

In June 2015 the company released Chainer, an open-source deep learning framework that influenced dynamic-graph design; development ended in December 2019 as the team moved to PyTorch. It announced the MN-Core accelerator in December 2018, and the MN-3 system topped the Green500 list in June 2020.
Preferred Networks continues to publish open code and Japanese language models, including the PLaMo family.
mission: The company aims to apply deep learning to real-world problems, combining software, custom hardware and large-scale computing.

tagline: A lab and compute platform working on distributed training, asynchronous reinforcement learning and open environments for agentic models.
about: Prime Intellect was co-founded by Vincent Weisser and Johannes Hagemann. Its 2024 launch post framed the company around open, decentralized AI development.

In late 2024 it released INTELLECT-1, a 10B-class model trained on 1 trillion tokens across nodes on three continents with its PRIME distributed training framework, together with data and checkpoints. The company now offers inference, GPU compute, sandboxes and a model factory.

Its open-source projects include prime-rl, a framework for asynchronous reinforcement learning at scale, and the Verifiers library with an Environments Hub that lists thousands of community environments.
mission: Prime Intellect pursues open, globally distributed AI development and wants individuals and small teams to be able to train and own capable models.

tagline: The Princeton NLP group, source of SWE-bench, SimPO and Tree of Thoughts, with many open benchmarks, methods and models.
about: Princeton NLP is the natural language processing research group at Princeton University. Its GitHub organization hosts widely used research code and its Hugging Face organization hosts models and datasets.

The group's SWE-bench benchmark, published at ICLR 2024, tests whether language models can resolve real GitHub issues and became a standard evaluation for coding agents. SimPO, presented at NeurIPS 2024, is a reference-free preference optimization method, and Tree of Thoughts (NeurIPS 2023) is a deliberate problem-solving framework for language models.
Karthik Narasimhan is among the authors of SWE-bench; Danqi Chen also leads work in the group.
mission: The group studies how language models learn, reason and act, and releases the resulting benchmarks and code for the community.

tagline: A Freiburg company behind TabPFN, the tabular foundation model published in Nature that predicts on structured data without task-specific training.
about: Prior Labs was founded by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann and Sauraj Gambhir to commercialize TabPFN, a transformer pretrained on synthetic data that handles tabular prediction in a single forward pass.

TabPFN was published in Nature in early 2025. The company raised a 9 million euro pre-seed round led by Balderton in February 2025, and its scientific advisory board includes Yann LeCun and Bernhard Schölkopf.
In May 2026 SAP announced plans to acquire Prior Labs, with commitments that it remains a separate legal entity and keeps its open-source work.
mission: Prior Labs wants foundation models to become the default tool for tabular data, which dominates business and science data.

tagline: A Paris mission-driven company spun out of Inria to sustain scikit-learn and the open-source data science ecosystem around it.
about: Probabl was formed by contributors to scikit-learn and other Inria-backed libraries so that these projects stay well maintained and funded. It launched around early 2024 with Yann Lechelle, formerly of Scaleway, as CEO.
Scikit-learn core maintainers employed by Inria joined as co-founders. Inria and the French state are shareholders, and the company has a mission-driven legal structure.
Sifted reported a 13 million euro seed round in October 2025.
mission: Probabl intends to make open-source machine learning tools sustainable and to offer professional services and products around them.

tagline: A Catalan government initiative led by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center that builds open Catalan language models, speech resources and corpora.
about: Projecte Aina is run by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with funding from the Government of Catalonia. A BSC paper describes it as a five-year project with 15 million euros that began in 2022.

The project has built what BSC describes as the largest Catalan text corpus and has started a Catalan speech corpus. Its models and datasets are published on Hugging Face, and the related Salamandra models were trained on the MareNostrum 5 supercomputer.
Its resources are intended for reuse by companies, public bodies and researchers.
mission: Aina aims to ensure that technology understands and speaks Catalan, with open resources that others can reuse.

tagline: A model efficiency company that open-sources the pruna framework for compressing and accelerating AI models.
about: Pruna AI was started by Bertrand Charpentier, John Rachwan, Rayan Nait Mazi and Stephan Günnemann, researchers in AI efficiency from TUM. John Rachwan is co-founder and CTO.

In March 2025 it open-sourced its optimization framework, which combines caching, pruning, quantization and distillation and checks quality loss. The pruna package is MIT-licensed, while a pro tier adds further methods.
The company also publishes many compressed models on Hugging Face.
mission: Pruna aims to make AI models smaller, faster and cheaper to run.

pyannoteAI was founded in 2024 with Vincent Molina as CEO and Bredin as chief science officer. It sells faster hosted models such as precision-2.
In late 2025 the project released pyannote.audio 4.0 with the open community-1 model.
mission: The team aims to give developers accurate speaker intelligence, keeping the core toolkit open while funding development through hosted models.

about: The Qatar Computing Research Institute is part of Hamad Bin Khalifa University and focuses on Arabic language technology, multilingual NLP and responsible AI.

It developed Fanar, a sovereign Arabic-centric platform covering language, speech and image generation, sponsored by Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. HBKU has since released Fanar 2.0. QCRI also hosts tools such as Farasa for Arabic processing.
The institute publishes research and releases code and models on GitHub and Hugging Face.
mission: QCRI works to advance Arabic AI and make language technology accessible for Arabic speakers.

In March 2025 it released Reka Flash 3, a 21B reasoning model trained with reinforcement learning (RLOO), under Apache 2.0. In July 2025 it open-sourced Reka Flash 3.1 and the Reka Quant quantization method.
It also publishes the Vibe-Eval benchmark for multimodal models.

tagline: A Japanese generative AI company known for releasing pretrained Japanese GPT, BERT and speech models, including the Youri and Nekomata LLMs.
about: rinna develops base models for Japanese text, audio and images, including GPT, BERT, HuBERT, CLIP and Stable Diffusion variants, and publishes them on Hugging Face.

Its Youri series continues pretraining of Llama 2 on about 40 billion tokens of mixed Japanese and English data, and the Nekomata series builds on Alibaba's Qwen models with a tokenizer more efficient for Japanese.
The company's early Japanese GPT-2 models became common baselines for Japanese NLP.
mission: rinna aims to give Japanese developers open pretrained models for their language.

about: Roboflow was started by Joseph Nelson (CEO) and Brad Dwyer (CTO) after their 2017 Magic Sudoku augmented reality app. The company's own site says they launched it in 2020, while other sources date incorporation to 2019.

Open-source projects include Supervision for vision utilities, Inference for running models, and RF-DETR, a real-time detector accepted at ICLR 2026. Roboflow Universe hosts shared datasets and models.
RF-DETR authors include Peter Robicheaux, James Gallagher and Isaac Robinson alongside Nelson.
mission: Roboflow wants to make computer vision accessible to every developer.

tagline: An open-source community behind the RWKV recurrent language model architecture, hosted as a Linux Foundation AI & Data project.
about: RWKV started as a project by independent researcher Bo Peng, who leads it, and grew into a community project under the Linux Foundation AI & Data.

The architecture has gone through versions named Dove, Eagle, Finch and Goose. RWKV-7 Goose, described in a March 2025 arXiv paper, generalizes the delta rule with vector-valued gating and supports state tracking. Models of 0.4B, 1.5B and 2.9B were released under Apache 2.0.
Contributors come from EleutherAI, Recursal AI and several universities.
mission: RWKV aims to offer an efficient alternative to transformers with linear-time inference.

about: Sakana AI was founded in 2023 by David Ha (CEO), Llion Jones (CTO) and Ren Ito (COO). Ha and Jones had worked at Google, where they met in Tokyo.

The lab pursues nature-inspired methods. Evolutionary Model Merge combines layers and weights of existing models without retraining, and The AI Scientist is a framework for automated scientific discovery.
It releases research code, models and Japanese datasets.
mission: Sakana AI aims to develop foundation models inspired by natural processes such as evolution and collective intelligence.

In April 2024 the group released Minerva, a family of language models trained from scratch on Italian and English, each on more than 500 billion words. The work was led by Navigli with Edoardo Barba and Simone Conia within the FAIR project, with CINECA compute.
The group publishes tools for entity linking, coreference and semantics.

The company says the models were trained from scratch, with 16T tokens for the 30B and 12T tokens for the 105B, and target Indian languages. Independent benchmarks from Artificial Analysis place the 105B below several peer open models.
Sarvam also builds speech and enterprise products.

tagline: A conversational speech company that open-sourced the CSM-1B base speech model while building voice companions.
about: Sesame builds conversational voice AI. In March 2025 it open-sourced CSM-1B, a base speech generation model pairing a Llama backbone with an audio decoder that produces Mimi audio codes.
The release is under Apache 2.0, with ethical use guidelines. The open checkpoint is a base model that has not been fine-tuned to a specific voice; a fine-tuned version powers the company's demo.
The listed authors include Johan Schalkwyk, Ankit Kumar, Dan Lyth and Zack Hodari.

The lab's Intern series includes InternLM multilingual foundation and chat models, InternVL multimodal models, and Intern-S1, a 241B-parameter mixture-of-experts scientific multimodal model with 28B parameters active per token, released under Apache 2.0.
It also open-sources a toolchain around these models.

Outputs included a Spanish NER model, a clinical text classifier and datasets such as DiagTrast. A 2024 arXiv paper describes the hackathon as a recurring international online event.

Stable Diffusion 1.5 (October 2022) became a foundation for community fine-tuning. Stable Diffusion 3.5 followed in late 2024 under a community licence free for those with under $1M annual revenue.

tagline: Stanford's Center for Research on Foundation Models, creators of the HELM evaluation framework and Alpaca.
about: CRFM is a Stanford HAI center directed by Percy Liang. It studies foundation models and builds open tools for evaluating them.

HELM, published in 2022, benchmarked 30 models on 42 scenarios and 7 metrics under standard conditions, and is maintained as a living benchmark. The center also produced Alpaca, a fine-tuned LLaMA 7B model.
It releases BioMedLM and training code on GitHub and Hugging Face.
mission: CRFM aims to make foundation models more transparent and understood through open evaluation and research.
